Here is a sample Semgrep rule in YAML format for the vulnerable function or method:

```yaml
---
id: "vuln-mcp-server-taskwarrior-1ee3d282"
title: "Potential Command Injection Vulnerability in Taskwarrior Server"
description: "This rule detects potential command injection vulnerabilities in the Taskwarrior server."
severity: WARNING
languages:
  - typescript
metadata:
  tags:
    - security
    - command-injection
  references:
    - https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/74.html
    - https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/77.html
pattern:
  - "function parseArgs(args) { (args|any).forEach((arg, index) => { if (index > 0 && arg.includes('`')) return; } }"
```

This rule will match any function named `parseArgs` that takes an array of arguments and checks each argument for the presence of a backtick (``). If such an argument is found, it's likely to be part of a command injection attack.

Please note that this is just a basic example and might not cover all possible vulnerabilities in your codebase. You should adjust the pattern according to your specific needs and the language you are using.
